title: A chipset's ITX token is the chipset (R1003)
body:
Implements `docs/plans/oracle/itx-chipset-variant.md` — **OD-7 / R1003**, evidence **BL-9**.

ITX boards are named `<chipset>I`, and the right-boundary rule means the chipset alias cannot see them. **The measured case is total:** a 33-minute review of the MSI MPG B850I Edge TI matched `B850` **zero** times, in title and body both — so even the automatic title include missed it. Every ITX review in the corpus is affected, and ITX is where one-DIMM-per-channel memory behaviour lives.

**A derived form, not a relaxed boundary.** Every declared surface form of a `kind = "chipset"` alias enters the pattern a second time with a trailing `i`. `theb850i` and `b850ix` still match nothing, and `asrocki` is still not ASRock — those negatives are the point.

**Derived from every declared form, not the canonical alone**, so a spelling you add later gets its ITX variant with no code change. That is the self-maintaining property OD-7 rejected hand-listed `b850i` entries for. Explicit still beats derived, and it falls out of the existing first-declared-wins rule rather than being a new one: declared forms are enumerated in full before any derived one.

**The threshold still gates bodies**, as OD-7 requires: an ITX video naming one chipset in its body is one distinct canonical and stays excluded at N=3. The title hit is what rescues the measured case.

**The blind tests found two defects in my implementation**, both fixed here rather than tested around:

1. `itx_forms` was private and `ITX_SUFFIX` did not exist. The plan's Signatures block declares both public **and says why** — "so the rule has a unit the tests can reach without asserting on the shape of the whole table's pattern" — which is precisely what I had made impossible.
2. `itx_forms` returned the same spelling twice when two declared forms normalize to one string (`b650` and `b 650` both fold to `b650`). The global de-duplication hid it, but a function returning a list of spellings that repeats itself has a dishonest contract.

The author also turned *"`aliases.toml` gains no new surface forms"* into an executable invariant: the intersection of declared normalized forms and derived forms over the shipped table must be empty. Stricter than "explicit beats derived" needs in general, and deliberate — OD-7 rejected hand-listing.

**The regression's title is a labelled reconstruction** (BL-18, LOW, proceeded on, under OD-17). The real title is in no commit, journal entry or run record; only BL-9's board name has measured provenance, and it is the only part asserted on.

Measured on the real corpus: **B650 title hits 4 → 7, X870 11 → 13**, and `aliases --check` now reports `b650i` and `x870i` among the forms that fired.

818 passing.
